name: OutSends
summary: Cold email platform for Gmail senders: contact management, campaigns with automated follow-ups, peer-to-peer warm-up and reporting, on flat plans metered by monthly emails and active contacts.
best_for: founders, freelancers and small agencies who run cold email from Gmail and want flat monthly plans by email volume, with warm-up and follow-up sequences included
skip_if: several people need their own logins and the $199 Team plan is more than you want to spend; you want a refund option before you commit; or you send a few hundred emails a month and a mail merge does the job
honest_knock: Paid fees are non-refundable, and every plan below the $199 Team / Agency plan has a single seat. The FAQ promises 100% primary inbox placement from its warm-up, which no sending tool controls. The cards do not name their currency, and annual totals were not shown to us.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-17 in a browser on outsends.com/pricing, monthly view; the cards show a $ sign without naming the currency, and the page says prices exclude VAT) Four fixed plans, each with unlimited campaigns, sequences and templates and no daily sending caps. Starter is $19 a month for 20,000 emails a month and 10,000 active contacts, 1 seat, 15 AI credits a day and 3 warm-up accounts. Pro is $49 for 100,000 emails and 50,000 contacts, 1 seat, 50 AI credits a day and 10 warm-up accounts. Growth is $99 for 200,000 emails and 100,000 contacts, 1 seat, 100 credits and 20 warm-up accounts. Team / Agency is $199 for 350,000 emails, 200,000 contacts, 10 team seats, 200 credits and 50 warm-up accounts. Starter keeps logs for 30 days, the others for 60. Above that, Custom starts at $300 a month for 300K to 2M+ emails at $1.00 per 1,000 emails. Annual billing is advertised as two months free, saving up to $398 a year; we did not get the annual totals to display, so check them at checkout. Monthly plans start with a 14-day free trial. The terms say paid fees are non-refundable unless the law requires otherwise, and a cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period.
